summary: Create runtime-ops Slack channel with automated thread->Confluence page creation and Jira escalation sync
description:
Issue summary: Request to provision a new #runtime-ops Slack channel that automatically converts any new top-level thread into a persistent Confluence page (under OPS > Runtime Incidents) and creates a Jira support task when a thread is flagged with :escalate: emoji. The automation should also surface a short digest to the channel nightly and allow timebound guest access for partner on-call rotation with approval.

Impact: Improves post-incident documentation hygiene and reduces manual ticket creation. Current pain: on-call posts incident notes in ephemeral channels, losing thread context; follow-up tickets are created manually leading to missed action items. This affects SRE, platform, and on-call rotations across pods.

Proposed solution:
- Create Slack channel #runtime-ops with topic and pinned runbooks.
- Install/configure a lightweight automation (Bolt/Workflow Builder or our internal bot) that: 
  * On new top-level thread post, create a Confluence draft page in Ops/Runtime Incidents with the thread title, timestamp, author, and initial messages.
  * On reaction :escalate: from any member, create a Jira task under project INT-OPS (use INT- prefix internal support) prefilled with thread link, Confluence draft link, urgency label, and assign to the on-call rotation.
  * On channel thread closure (no activity for 48h), auto-publish the Confluence draft and add page to the weekly incident index.
- Implement an approval flow for external guest access (timebound 7-day window) via our existing provision bot; ensure guests are not able to see confidential Confluence pages unless whitelisted.
- Nightly digest: post a short list of threads created that day with links to Confluence pages and Jira tasks.

Acceptance criteria:
- #runtime-ops exists and is discoverable in Slack.
- New thread in channel creates a Confluence draft with correct metadata within 2 minutes.
- Reacting with :escalate: generates a Jira task with required fields and links.
- Drafts auto-publish after 48h of inactivity and appear in the incident index.
- Guest access requests route through the approval bot and enforce timebound scopes.
- No elevation of Confluence visibility occurs for drafts; only published pages follow space permissions.

Steps to reproduce (for testing):
1) Post a new top-level thread in #runtime-ops with incident title.
2) Verify Confluence draft appears at the linked page URL and contains thread content.
3) Add :escalate: reaction from another user.
4) Confirm Jira task creation with links.
5) Leave thread idle and confirm auto-publish after 48h or trigger manual publish via command.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: accidental exposure of private data in Confluence draft. Mitigation: drafts created in restricted Ops space; only on-publish do we inherit normal space permissions. Add a pre-publish checklist that requires a reviewer.
- Risk: spam creating many drafts. Mitigation: rate-limit automation (3 drafts per user per day) and provide a manual opt-out command.

Rollout plan:
- Stage in staging workspace for 1 week with Platform pod and Oncall team testing.
- After signoff, enable in prod for limited audience (SRE + Platform) for 2 weeks.
- Open to all runtime-related owners after monitoring.

Follow-ups:
- Create a small dashboard in Console tracking drafts->published ratio and average time-to-ticket.
- Add training snippet to the on-call runbook.
